sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam viśvāmitrasya saṃvādaṃ caṇḍālasya ca pakkaṇe
english: On this very matter they recite an ancient tale: the dialogue between Viśvāmitra and a Caṇḍāla in his hamlet.

sanskrit: tretādvāparayoḥ saṃdhau purā daivavidhikramāt anāvṛṣṭir abhūd ghorā rājan dvādaśavārṣikī
english: At the juncture of the Tretā and the Dvāpara ages, long ago, by the ordained course of fate, there fell a fearful drought, O king, lasting twelve years.

sanskrit: prajānām abhivṛddhānāṃ yugānte paryupasthite tretānirmokṣasamaye dvāparapratipādane
english: When the creatures had multiplied and the close of the age drew near, at the time of the Tretā's passing and the ushering in of the Dvāpara,

sanskrit: na vavarṣa sahasrākṣaḥ pratilomo 'bhavad guruḥ jagāma dakṣiṇaṃ mārgaṃ somo vyāvṛttalakṣaṇaḥ
english: the thousand-eyed Indra rained not; the planet Bṛhaspati turned contrary; and the Moon, his marks reversed, went the southern path.

sanskrit: nāvaśyāyo 'pi rātryante kuta evābhrarājayaḥ nadyaḥ saṃkṣiptatoyaughāḥ kva cid antargatābhavan
english: At the end of night there was not even dew, let alone ranks of clouds; the rivers, their flooding waters shrunk away, in places sank wholly underground.

sanskrit: sarāṃsi saritaś caiva kūpāḥ prasravaṇāni ca hatatviṭkāny alakṣyanta nisargād daivakāritāt
english: Lakes and streams, wells and springs alike were seen stripped of their luster, drained of their nature by the working of fate.

sanskrit: upaśuṣkajalasthāyā vinivṛttasabhāprapā nivṛttayajñasvādhyāyā nirvaṣaṭkāramaṅgalā
english: The land's water-resting places were dried up; its halls and watering-booths abandoned; its sacrifices and Vedic recitation ceased; its auspicious cries of vaṣaṭ fallen silent.

sanskrit: utsannakṛṣigorakṣyā nivṛttavipaṇāpaṇā nivṛttapūgasamayā saṃpranaṣṭamahotsavā
english: Tillage and the keeping of cattle had collapsed; buying and selling in the markets had stopped; the gatherings of the guilds had ended; the great festivals were utterly lost.

sanskrit: asthikaṅkālasaṃkīrṇā hāhābhūtajanākulā śūnyabhūyiṣṭhanagarā dagdhagrāmaniveśanā
english: The earth was strewn with bones and skeletons, thronged with people crying alas; her cities mostly emptied, her village-dwellings burned to ash.

sanskrit: kva cic coraiḥ kva cic chastraiḥ kva cid rājabhir āturaiḥ parasparabhayāc caiva śūnyabhūyiṣṭhanirjanā
english: Here by thieves, there by the sword, elsewhere by desperate kings, and through mutual terror besides, she was left for the most part empty and unpeopled.

sanskrit: gatadaivatasaṃkalpā vṛddhabālavinākṛtā gojāvimahiṣair hīnā parasparaharāharā
english: Her resolve in the gods departed, bereft of her old folk and her children, stripped of cattle, goats, and buffalo, men plundering one another in turn,

sanskrit: hataviprā hatārakṣā pranaṣṭauṣadhisaṃcayā śyāvabhūtanaraprāyā babhūva vasudhā tadā
english: her brahmins slain, her safeguards slain, her stores of herbs all perished, peopled mostly by men turned ashen-gray—such did the earth become in that hour.

sanskrit: tasmin pratibhaye kāle kṣīṇe dharme yudhiṣṭhira babhramuḥ kṣudhitā martyāḥ khādantaḥ sma parasparam
english: In that dreadful season, when dharma had waned, O Yudhiṣṭhira, famished mortals wandered, devouring one another.

sanskrit: ṛṣayo niyamāṃs tyaktvā parityaktāgnidaivatāḥ āśramān saṃparityajya paryadhāvann itas tataḥ
english: The sages, casting off their vows, forsaking their sacred fires and their gods, abandoned their hermitages and ran about hither and thither.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'tha bhagavān maharṣir aniketanaḥ kṣudhā parigato dhīmān samantāt paryadhāvata
english: Then the venerable Viśvāmitra, the great seer, himself without a home, beset by hunger though wise, ran roaming on every side.

sanskrit: sa kadā cit paripatañ śvapacānāṃ niveśanam hiṃsrāṇāṃ prāṇihantṝṇām āsasāda vane kva cit
english: Once, as he strayed about, he came upon the settlement of dog-cookers—savage men, slayers of living creatures—somewhere in the forest.

sanskrit: vibhinnakalaśākīrṇaṃ śvacarmācchādanāyutam varāhakharabhagnāsthikapālaghaṭasaṃkulam
english: It was littered with broken pots, draped about with dog-skins, crowded with the cracked bones of boars and asses, with skulls and crocks.

sanskrit: mṛtacelaparistīrṇaṃ nirmālyakṛtabhūṣaṇam sarpanirmokamālābhiḥ kṛtacihnakuṭīmaṭham
english: It was spread over with the garments of the dead, its ornaments made of cast-off funeral flowers, its huts and shrines marked out with garlands of shed snake-skins.

sanskrit: ulūkapakṣadhvajibhir devatāyatanair vṛtam lohaghaṇṭāpariṣkāraṃ śvayūthaparivāritam
english: It was hemmed about with godlings' shrines, their banners owl-feathered, decked out with iron bells and ringed about with packs of dogs.

sanskrit: tat praviśya kṣudhāviṣṭo gādheḥ putro mahān ṛṣiḥ āhārānveṣaṇe yuktaḥ paraṃ yatnaṃ samāsthitaḥ
english: Entering it, overpowered by hunger, the great seer, son of Gādhi, intent on his search for food, set himself to the utmost effort.

sanskrit: na ca kva cid avindat sa bhikṣamāṇo 'pi kauśikaḥ māṃsam annaṃ mūlaphalam anyad vā tatra kiṃ cana
english: Yet nowhere, for all his begging, did Kauśika find any flesh, any grain, any root or fruit, or aught else whatever there.

sanskrit: aho kṛcchraṃ mayā prāptam iti niścitya kauśikaḥ papāta bhūmau daurbalyāt tasmiṃś caṇḍālapakkaṇe
english: "Alas, into what straits I have come!"—so resolving, Kauśika sank to the earth from weakness there in that Caṇḍāla hamlet.

sanskrit: cintayām āsa sa muniḥ kiṃ nu me sukṛtaṃ bhavet kathaṃ vṛthā na mṛtyuḥ syād iti pārthivasattama
english: The sage fell to pondering: "What now would be the right thing for me to do? How might my death not be in vain?"—so, O best of kings.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa śvamāṃsasya kutantīṃ vitatāṃ muniḥ caṇḍālasya gṛhe rājan sadyaḥ śastrahatasya ca
english: And the sage caught sight of a haunch of dog's flesh stretched out, in the Caṇḍāla's hut, O king—flesh of a creature freshly killed by the blade.

sanskrit: sa cintayām āsa tadā steyaṃ kāryam ito mayā na hīdānīm upāyo 'nyo vidyate prāṇadhāraṇe
english: Then he reflected: "Theft must I commit from this place, for now no other means whatever exists to keep my life.

sanskrit: āpatsu vihitaṃ steyaṃ viśiṣṭasamahīnataḥ paraṃ paraṃ bhavet pūrvam asteyam iti niścayaḥ
english: In dire need theft is sanctioned—from a superior, an equal, or a lower man; yet it grows ever graver in that order, and this is the rule: first do no theft at all.

sanskrit: hīnād ādeyam ādau syāt samānāt tadanantaram asaṃbhavād ādadīta viśiṣṭād api dhārmikāt
english: What is taken should first be taken from a lower man, then from an equal; and only when no other course remains may one take even from a superior and righteous person.

sanskrit: so 'ham antāvasānānāṃ haramāṇaḥ parigrahāt na steyadoṣaṃ paśyāmi hariṣyāmy etad āmiṣam
english: I, then, in taking from the possession of these lowest of the low, see no guilt of theft; this meat I shall take."

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhiṃ samāsthāya viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ tasmin deśe prasuṣvāpa patito yatra bhārata
english: Fixed in this resolve, the great sage Viśvāmitra slept where he had fallen, in that very spot, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa vigāḍhāṃ niśāṃ dṛṣṭvā supte caṇḍālapakkaṇe śanair utthāya bhagavān praviveśa kuṭīmaṭham
english: Seeing the night well advanced, while the Caṇḍāla hamlet slept, the venerable one rose softly and stole into the hut and its shrine.

sanskrit: sa supta eva caṇḍālaḥ śleṣmāpihitalocanaḥ paribhinnasvaro rūkṣa uvācāpriyadarśanaḥ
english: But the Caṇḍāla, though still asleep, his eyes gummed shut with rheum, harsh, his voice cracking, a man grim to look upon, spoke out:

sanskrit: kaḥ kutantīṃ ghaṭṭayati supte caṇḍālapakkaṇe jāgarmi nāvasupto 'smi hato 'sīti ca dāruṇaḥ
english: "Who tampers with the haunch while the Caṇḍāla hamlet sleeps? I am awake, I am not sound asleep—you are a dead man!"—so cried the fierce fellow.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'ham ity eva sahasā tam uvāca saḥ sahasābhyāgatabhayaḥ sodvegas tena karmaṇā
english: "I am Viśvāmitra"—so on the instant he answered him, fear coming upon him all at once, agitated by that deed.

sanskrit: caṇḍālas tad vacaḥ śrutvā maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ śayanād upasaṃbhrānta iyeṣotpatituṃ tataḥ
english: When the Caṇḍāla heard that speech of the great seer of disciplined soul, startled, he sought to spring up at once from his bed.

sanskrit: sa visṛjyāśru netrābhyāṃ bahumānāt kṛtāñjaliḥ uvāca kauśikaṃ rātrau brahman kiṃ te cikīrṣitam
english: Shedding tears from his eyes, with reverence and folded hands, he said to Kauśika in the night: "Brahmin, what is it you mean to do?"

sanskrit: viśvāmitras tu mātaṅgam uvāca parisāntvayan kṣudhito 'haṃ gataprāṇo hariṣyāmi śvajāghanīm
english: And Viśvāmitra, soothing the outcaste, said: "I am starving, my life ebbing away; I mean to take this haunch of dog.

sanskrit: avasīdanti me prāṇāḥ smṛtir me naśyati kṣudhā svadharmaṃ budhyamāno 'pi hariṣyāmi śvajāghanīm
english: My life-breaths fail; my memory perishes from hunger; and though I know full well my own dharma, I shall take this haunch of dog.

sanskrit: aṭan bhaikṣaṃ na vindāmi yadā yuṣmākam ālaye tadā buddhiḥ kṛtā pāpe hariṣyāmi śvajāghanīm
english: When, roaming for alms, I find nothing here in your dwelling, then is my mind set upon this sin: I shall take the haunch of dog.

sanskrit: tṛṣitaḥ kaluṣaṃ pātā nāsti hrīr aśanārthinaḥ kṣud dharmaṃ dūṣayaty atra hariṣyāmi śvajāghanīm
english: A man parched will drink foul water; for one seeking food there is no shame; here hunger corrupts dharma—I shall take the haunch of dog."

sanskrit: agnir mukhaṃ purodhāś ca devānāṃ śucipād vibhuḥ yathā sa sarvabhug brahmā tathā māṃ viddhi dharmataḥ
english: "Agni is the mouth and the household priest of the gods, the pure-footed lord; even as he, the all-devourer, is Brahman, so know me to be by the law."

sanskrit: tam uvāca sa caṇḍālo maharṣe śṛṇu me vacaḥ śrutvā tathā samātiṣṭha yathā dharmān na hīyase
english: To him the Caṇḍāla replied: "Great seer, hear my words, and when you have heard, so order yourself that you fall not away from dharma.

sanskrit: mṛgāṇām adhamaṃ śvānaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ tasyāpy adhama uddeśaḥ śarīrasyorujāghanī
english: The wise declare the dog the basest of beasts; and basest even of its body is this part, the haunch of its thigh.

sanskrit: nedaṃ samyag vyavasitaṃ maharṣe karma vaikṛtam caṇḍālasvasya haraṇam abhakṣyasya viśeṣataḥ
english: This is no rightly resolved purpose, O great seer—a deed perverse: the stealing of a Caṇḍāla's property, and that of food unfit to eat besides.

sanskrit: sādhv anyam anupaśya tvam upāyaṃ prāṇadhāraṇe na māṃsalobhāt tapaso nāśas te syān mahāmune
english: Look rather, I pray, for some other means to sustain your life; let there be no ruin of your austerity through greed for meat, O great sage.

sanskrit: jānato 'vihito mārgo na kāryo dharmasaṃkaraḥ mā sma dharmaṃ parityākṣīs tvaṃ hi dharmavid uttamaḥ
english: For one who knows, the unsanctioned path is not to be taken; the confounding of dharma must not be wrought. Forsake not dharma—you, the foremost of those who know it."

sanskrit: viśvāmitras tato rājann ity ukto bharatarṣabha kṣudhārtaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ punar eva mahāmuniḥ
english: Then, O king, bull of the Bhāratas, thus addressed, Viśvāmitra the great sage, tormented by hunger, answered him once again:

sanskrit: nirāhārasya sumahān mama kālo 'bhidhāvataḥ na vidyate 'bhyupāyaś ca kaś cin me prāṇadhāraṇe
english: "A very long time has passed for me without food as I have run about, and no means whatever is to be found for sustaining my life.

sanskrit: yena tena viśeṣeṇa karmaṇā yena kena cit abhyujjīvet sīdamānaḥ samartho dharmam ācaret
english: By this means or that, by whatever deed soever, the man who is sinking should keep himself alive; once able, he may then practice dharma.

sanskrit: aindro dharmaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānām athāgnikaḥ brahmavahnir mama balaṃ bhakṣyāmi samayaṃ kṣudhā
english: Indra's is the dharma of the Kṣatriyas, the fire-god's that of the brahmins; the fire of Brahman is my strength—in this strait I shall eat, driven by hunger.

sanskrit: yathā yathā vai jīved dhi tat kartavyam apīḍayā jīvitaṃ maraṇāc chreyo jīvan dharmam avāpnuyāt
english: By whatever means one may live, that very thing must be done, without affliction; life is better than death—living, a man may yet attain dharma.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ jīvitam ākāṅkṣann abhakṣasyāpi bhakṣaṇam vyavasye buddhipūrvaṃ vai tad bhavān anumanyatām
english: I, therefore, longing to live, resolve, with full deliberation, to eat even this food unfit to be eaten; let your honor consent to it."

sanskrit: jīvan dharmaṃ cariṣyāmi praṇotsyāmy aśubhāni ca tapobhir vidyayā caiva jyotīṃṣīva mahat tamaḥ
english: "Living, I shall practice dharma and shall drive off my evils by austerities and by knowledge, as lights drive off the great darkness."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca naitat khādan prāpsyase prāṇam anyaṃ; nāyur dīrghaṃ nāmṛtasyeva tṛptim bhikṣām anyāṃ bhikṣa mā te mano 'stu; śvabhakṣaṇe śvā hy abhakṣo dvijānām
english: The dog-cooker said: "By eating this you will gain no other life, no long span of days, nor any fullness as of the nectar of immortality. Beg some other alms; let not your mind be set on eating dog—for the dog is no food for the twice-born."

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca na durbhikṣe sulabhaṃ māṃsam anyac; chvapāka nānnaṃ na ca me 'sti vittam kṣudhārtaś cāham agatir nirāśaḥ; śvamāṃse cāsmin ṣaḍrasān sādhu manye
english: Viśvāmitra said: "In this famine no other flesh is easy to come by, O dog-cooker, nor grain, nor have I any wealth. Tormented by hunger, helpless, without hope, I deem this dog's flesh to hold the six savors well enough."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca pañca pañcanakhā bhakṣyā brahmakṣatrasya vai dvija yadi śāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te mābhakṣye mānasaṃ kṛthāḥ
english: The dog-cooker said: "Five among the five-clawed beasts are fit to eat for the brahmin and the kṣatriya, O twice-born; if the scripture is your authority, set not your mind upon what may not be eaten."

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca agastyenāsuro jagdho vātāpiḥ kṣudhitena vai aham āpadgataḥ kṣubdho bhakṣayiṣye śvajāghanīm
english: Viśvāmitra said: "The demon Vātāpi was once devoured by Agastya in his hunger; I, fallen into calamity and shaken, shall eat the haunch of dog."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca bhikṣām anyām āhareti na caitat kartum arhasi na nūnaṃ kāryam etad vai hara kāmaṃ śvajāghanīm
english: The dog-cooker said: "'Fetch some other alms'—so I say; you ought not to do this thing. Surely this is not to be done; yet take the haunch of dog, if you will."

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca śiṣṭā vai kāraṇaṃ dharme tadvṛttam anuvartaye parāṃ medhyāśanād etāṃ bhakṣyāṃ manye śvajāghanīm
english: Viśvāmitra said: "The cultured are the warrant in matters of dharma; their conduct I would follow. Better than eating pure food I deem this haunch of dog to be, here, a thing fit to be eaten."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca asatā yat samācīrṇaṃ na sa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ nāvṛttam anukāryaṃ vai mā chalenānṛtaṃ kṛthāḥ
english: The dog-cooker said: "What is practiced by the base is no eternal dharma; what is not the established usage is not to be imitated. Do not by sophistry make a lie of the truth."

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca na pātakaṃ nāvamatam ṛṣiḥ san kartum arhasi samau ca śvamṛgau manye tasmād bhakṣyā śvajāghanī
english: Viśvāmitra said: "Being a seer, you ought to do nothing fallen, nothing despised; yet I hold the dog and the deer to be alike, and therefore the haunch of dog fit to be eaten."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca yad brāhmaṇārthe kṛtam arthitena; tenarṣiṇā tac ca bhakṣyādhikāram sa vai dharmo yatra na pāpam asti; sarvair upāyair hi sa rakṣitavyaḥ
english: The dog-cooker said: "What is done for a brahmin's sake by a seer in his need—that too carries the sanction to be eaten. But that alone is dharma in which there is no sin, and it is to be guarded by every means."

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca mitraṃ ca me brāhmaṇaś cāyam ātmā; priyaś ca me pūjyatamaś ca loke taṃ bhartukāmo 'ham imāṃ hariṣye; nṛśaṃsānām īdṛśānāṃ na bibhye
english: Viśvāmitra said: "This brahmin is my friend, my very self, dear to me and most worthy of honor in the world; wishing to sustain him, I shall take this haunch—of cruel men such as these I have no fear."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca kāmaṃ narā jīvitaṃ saṃtyajanti; na cābhakṣyaiḥ pratikurvanti tatra sarvān kāmān prāpnuvantīha vidvan; priyasva kāmaṃ sahitaḥ kṣudhā vai
english: The dog-cooker said: "Gladly do men give up their very lives, and do not redress their straits with forbidden food; and so, O learned one, they win here all their desires. Endure your hunger, then, if you must, holding fast."

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca sthāne tāvat saṃśayaḥ pretyabhāve; niḥsaṃśayaṃ karmaṇāṃ vā vināśaḥ ahaṃ punar varta ity āśayātmā; mūlaṃ rakṣan bhakṣayiṣyāmy abhakṣyam
english: Viśvāmitra said: "There is, to be sure, doubt about the state after death; but the loss of one's deeds is beyond doubt. With my heart set on this—'I may yet come back'—and guarding the root of life, I shall eat the forbidden food."

sanskrit: buddhyātmake vyastam astīti tuṣṭo; mohād ekatvaṃ yathā carma cakṣuḥ yady apy enaḥ saṃśayād ācarāmi; nāhaṃ bhaviṣyāmi yathā tvam eva
english: "He is content who knows the manifold to be set out within the realm of intellect, while through delusion oneness appears, as the skin and the eye are taken as one. And even if from doubt I commit a sin, I shall not become such as you yourself are."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca patanīyam idaṃ duḥkham iti me vartate matiḥ duṣkṛtī brāhmaṇaṃ santaṃ yas tvām aham upālabhe
english: The dog-cooker said: "This is a grief that brings about my fall—so runs my thought—that I, an evildoer, should reprove you who are a true brahmin."

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca pibanty evodakaṃ gāvo maṇḍūkeṣu ruvatsv api na te 'dhikāro dharme 'sti mā bhūr ātmapraśaṃsakaḥ
english: Viśvāmitra said: "The cattle drink the water even while the frogs croak on. You have no warrant in matters of dharma; do not be a praiser of yourself."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca suhṛd bhūtvānuśāsmi tvā kṛpā hi tvayi me dvija tad evaṃ śreya ādhatsva mā lobhāc chvānam ādithāḥ
english: The dog-cooker said: "It is as a well-wisher that I counsel you, for I feel compassion toward you, O twice-born. Lay hold, then, of what is for your good; take not the dog from greed."

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca suhṛn me tvaṃ sukhepsuś ced āpado māṃ samuddhara jāne 'haṃ dharmato ''tmānaṃ śvānīm utsṛja jāghanīm
english: Viśvāmitra said: "If you are my well-wisher, desiring my welfare, then rescue me from calamity. I know myself by the law; let go your hold upon the dog's haunch."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca naivotsahe bhavate dātum etāṃ; nopekṣituṃ hriyamāṇaṃ svam annam ubhau syāvaḥ svamalenāvaliptau; dātāhaṃ ca tvaṃ ca vipra pratīcchan
english: The dog-cooker said: "I have no heart to give you this, nor yet to look on idly while my own food is carried off; both of us would be smeared with our own defilement—I as the giver, and you, O brahmin, as the one who takes it."

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca adyāham etad vṛjinaṃ karma kṛtvā; jīvaṃś cariṣyāmi mahāpavitram prapūtātmā dharmam evābhipatsye; yad etayor guru tad vai bravīhi
english: Viśvāmitra said: "Today, having done this crooked deed, I shall live and practice the great purification; and with my soul made wholly pure, I shall lay hold of dharma itself. Tell me, then, which of these two is the weightier."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca ātmaiva sākṣī kila lokakṛtye; tvam eva jānāsi yad atra duṣṭam yo hy ādriyed bhakṣyam iti śvamāṃsaṃ; manye na tasyāsti vivarjanīyam
english: The dog-cooker said: "The self alone, they say, is witness in the works of the world; you yourself know what is wrong herein. As for him who would honor dog's flesh as food fit to eat—for him, I think, there is nothing left to shun."

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca upādāne khādane vāsya doṣaḥ; kāryo nyāyair nityam atrāpavādaḥ yasmin na hiṃsā nānṛte vākyaleśo; bhakṣyakriyā tatra na tad garīyaḥ
english: Viśvāmitra said: "Whether in the taking of this or in the eating of it lie a fault, the exception to the rule must ever be reasoned out by the canons of right. Where there is no harm done and no shred of falsehood in speech, there the act of eating is no grave thing."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca yady eṣa hetus tava khādanasya; na te vedaḥ kāraṇaṃ nānyadharmaḥ tasmād abhakṣye bhakṣaṇād vā dvijendra; doṣaṃ na paśyāmi yathedam āttha
english: The dog-cooker said: "If this is your reasoning for eating it, then neither the Veda nor any other dharma is your warrant; and so, O chief of the twice-born, in eating what may not be eaten I see no fault, just as you have said."

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca na pātakaṃ bhakṣaṇam asya dṛṣṭaṃ; surāṃ pītvā patatītīha śabdaḥ anyonyakarmāṇi tathā tathaiva; na leśamātreṇa kṛtyaṃ hinasti
english: Viśvāmitra said: "The eating of this is not seen to be a deadly sin; the dictum here runs, 'By drinking spirits one falls.' Each several deed has its own measure, just so; and a mere trifle does not undo the rightful act."

sanskrit: śvapaca uvāca asthānato hīnataḥ kutsitād vā; taṃ vidvāṃsaṃ bādhate sādhuvṛttam sthānaṃ punar yo labhate niṣaṅgāt; tenāpi daṇḍaḥ sahitavya eva
english: The dog-cooker said: "From an improper place, from a lower man, or from a thing reviled—such a taking afflicts even the learned man of good conduct. And he who recovers his standing through attachment must yet endure the penalty even so."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktvā nivavṛte mātaṅgaḥ kauśikaṃ tadā viśvāmitro jahāraiva kṛtabuddhiḥ śvajāghanīm
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus, the outcaste then desisted from Kauśika; and Viśvāmitra, his mind made up, took the haunch of dog after all.

sanskrit: tato jagrāha pañcāṅgīṃ jīvitārthī mahāmuniḥ sadāras tām upākṛtya vane yāto mahāmuniḥ
english: Then the great sage, bent on living, seized the five-membered haunch; and having prepared it, he went off with his wife into the forest, that great sage.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu pravavarṣātha vāsavaḥ saṃjīvayan prajāḥ sarvā janayām āsa cauṣadhīḥ
english: But at that very time Vāsava sent down his rain, bringing all creatures back to life, and made the healing herbs to grow again.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'pi bhagavāṃs tapasā dagdhakilbiṣaḥ kālena mahatā siddhim avāpa paramādbhutām
english: And the venerable Viśvāmitra too, his guilt burned away by austerity, in the course of long time attained a perfection most wondrous.
